evidence.text: Customers have firmed their capex since ASML's 15 July print, and this supports a Q4 guide at or above the ~EUR 14.2B the FY guide implies, plus a strong first 2027 statement. TSMC raised its 2026 capex to $60-64B from ~$56B on 16 July and said 3-year capex would be 'significantly higher'. TSMC's Q3 revenue of NT$1.494T beat the top of its guide (Sept monthly report, 8 Oct). Micron guided H1 FY27 capex to ~$25B against $27.4B for all of FY26 (late Sept). Samsung pre-announced a record Q3 operating profit of KRW 107.4T against a KRW 106.64T consensus (8 Oct). All of this came after ASML last spoke, and the 2027 consensus of ~EUR 54.7B (+24%) may not fully reflect it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (15 Jul): FY guide raised from EUR 36-40B to 43-45B plus the 2027 capacity plan, stock +2.23%. Q1 2026 (15 Apr): FY raised, stock -2.41% because the China share shrank. Oct 2025: a 2026 'not below 2025' statement, stock +2.71%. Jul 2025: 2026 growth not confirmed, stock -8.33%. The forward statement is the line this name trades on, and it is asymmetric: a withheld growth confirmation costs far more than a confirmation pays.
evidence.why_not_priced: Each datum is public, and the read-through to ASML's Q4 guide and 2027 number is the market's job. But the stock fell 7.4% in the 5 days into the print on sector AI-financing worries, not on any ASML datum, while the customer series improved. If the market had priced the customer data, ASML would not be trading below its gamma flip with 2027 consensus at only +24% while the brokers' WFE estimates sit at +38%.
evidence.independence: These are separate counterparty documents. Micron capex: https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10890090 . Samsung Q3 guidance (2026-10-08): https://www.samsung.com/global/ir/reports-disclosures/public-disclosure-view.84775/ . TSMC September revenue (2026-10-08): https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3343 . They are proxies for ASML's order book, not ASML's own numbers.

evidence.text: The 2027 bar has been raised by the sell side since July, so a qualitative 'strong growth' statement may not clear it. JPMorgan lifted 2027 WFE to +38% ($224.5B) on 18-19 Sept, citing DRAM and TSMC capex; Goldman lifted 2027 WFE growth to +45% and Morgan Stanley to $202B. The JPM note expects ASML to give initial 2027 guidance with Q3. ASML's own 2027 framework is +30% low-NA EUV units (~65 to ~85) and +30% DUV immersion, with 2027 low-NA 'close to fully covered'. Against WFE at +38-45%, a 2027 ASML statement of +20-25% would read as share loss or as a capacity ceiling.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the first-look forward statement: Oct 2025 (+2.71%) cleared a low bar, and Jul 2025 (-8.33%) missed it. Here the bar is high and set by broker WFE numbers, not by the company.
evidence.why_not_priced: This sets the expectation rather than being an unpriced fact. It enters only through the gap between broker WFE growth (+38-45%) and ASML's capacity-bound unit growth (+30%) plus pricing. If the market already expected ASML to grow below WFE, 2027 consensus would not have drifted up with the WFE revisions (11 up, 0 down on Q3 estimates in 30 days per 24/7 Wall St).

evidence.text: Pricing power has widened since July, a 2027 margin lever. The Elec, relayed around 9-10 Oct 2026, reports that ASML will raise spare-part prices for EUV and DUV tools by a uniform 10% for Samsung and SK hynix from January 2027, and that both accepted. That followed The Information's 15 July report that some Chinese customers accepted a ~10% price rise on mature DUV tools. On the Q2 call the CFO cited 'better pricing power'. ASML has not confirmed either report.

evidence.why_not_priced: A Korean trade-press scoop from four days before the print, landing in a week when the whole sector sold off. It only reaches the price if management quantifies or confirms it, for example in a 2027 GM comment. Had it been priced, 2027 GM expectations would sit above the Q3/Q4 ~56% run-rate, and no source found says they do.

evidence.text: The tape into the print is fragile, and the reaction function on good forward news is damped. Starting 8 Oct, chip stocks sold off on AI-financing worries (an OpenAI financing report, the Philadelphia semiconductor index -3.4% that day). Rates and oil above $105 added pressure, and the CXMT/China competition worry returned. ASML fell 1.7% on 12 Oct and 3.1% on 13 Oct, closing at $1,697.79 (-7.4% over 5 days), below the cited $1,735.79 gamma flip and at the $1,700 put wall. Bloomberg (13 Oct) framed ASML's guidance as key to restoring confidence in a 'fragile chip trade'. In that tape a confirming print can be sold, as in July 2025, and a strong one can trigger a relief move. On net, the sector beta carries a slight downward lean.

evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price; this finding is about how the print will be received, not about new information. The baseline's upside-paid skew suggests options are positioned for a relief rally. If sector beta were fully priced out, the stock would not be trading on the same day's Kospi -5.5% and SOX moves.

evidence.text: LME zinc ran to a roughly four-year high during AZZ's fiscal Q2 (Jun-Aug 2026): $3,634/t on 2026-08-04, about $3,746 on 08-06, about $3,900 cash by 2026-09-01, up more than 25% YTD on low LME stocks. On the 2026-07-09 call management said Metal Coatings surcharges are in place because zinc is high and that 'you're going to see the surcharge impact flowing through in sales'. Zinc bought today reaches the kettles 6-8 months later (FIFO, per the 10-Q). Q2 sales therefore carry surcharges priced off current zinc while cost of sales carries zinc bought around Dec 2025 to Feb 2026 at lower prices. That is a tailwind to Metal Coatings revenue and margin against a Q1 segment EBITDA margin of 30.3% and 30.8% in Q2 FY26.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Metal Coatings margin fell 260bp in Q1 FY27 (land-sale comparison, project mix), and the July beat-and-raise still closed -1.88%. In Q2 FY26 the segment margin was down 90bp and the stock fell -4.9% on a revenue miss. This name has not reliably paid for beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: The zinc price is public, but the sell-side has to model both the surcharge timing and the 6-8 month kettle lag. If the market had fully priced a margin tailwind, the stock would not sit 13.8% below its high with puts bid +10 vol points into the print. Part of the surcharge revenue is probably already in the $462M consensus, which is why this is sized small.

evidence.text: The Atlantic season had no hurricane through all of September 2026: the longest hurricane-free stretch in about 60 years, and the first hurricane (Isaias) formed only in October. evidence.text: Florida's excess-profits statute (s.627.066) tests 'any three-calendar-year period'. PGR booked $950M of policyholder credit expense in September 2025 for 2023-25 (CR 100.4 that month, stock -5.78%), cited the absence of 2025 Florida hurricanes as a driver, and recorded $1.224B for the full year 2025. The August 2026 release shows no policyholder credit expense in 2026 year to date, so with no Florida hurricane again in 2026 a catch-up accrual for 2024-26 could land in September as it did last year. That would take a large share of a roughly $1.10 September EPS bar.

evidence.text: At Barclays on 2026-09-14, CFO John Woods raised the FY26 fee revenue guide to +13-14% (from +12-13%) and put NII at the upper end of +14-15%. He called Q3 'stable vs Q2' across fees, NII and expenses, said servicing and management fees were running better than modelled while markets businesses moderated, and said expenses would be 'slightly higher'. Q3 consensus already sits on this: fees $3.20B vs about $3.19B in Q2, NII $858M vs $860M. The print lands inside what the company guided; the upside is only in the 'better than modelled' servicing and management fees.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 beat ($3.65 vs $3.34, revenue $4.05B vs $3.88B) and full-year raise: -0.50% (baseline). 5 of the last 7 prints fell; January 2026 -6.07% and July 2025 -7.29% (lines not identified).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It was public intra-quarter guidance and consensus EPS moved up 0.6% in 30 days. If the market had also priced the 'better than modelled' servicing and management fees, consensus fees would sit above the Q2 run-rate rather than flat on it ($3.20B vs about $3.19B). The stock fell about 7% after the raise, so the guide raise bought nothing on the tape.
evidence.independence: Peer read-through in finding 2 points the same way (Citi Securities Services +4% QoQ). Same-document caveat: the 'slightly higher' expense guide and the 'moderation in markets' remark come from this same transcript and are netted into this size, not filed separately.

evidence.text: Citi's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-13, after State Street last spoke) shows Securities Services revenue $1,712M, +13% YoY and +4% QoQ. NII was +7% QoQ ($801M vs $750M) and non-interest revenue +2% QoQ ($911M vs $893M), on AUC/A up 16% YoY. Services average deposits were +2% QoQ, and Markets FX revenue grew on higher volumes. A direct custody peer therefore grew sequentially in fees and NII, while State Street's consensus is flat QoQ on both (fees $3.20B vs about $3.19B, NII $858M vs $860M). JPM's same-day release shows deposits +2% QoQ and NII +6% QoQ firmwide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: State Street's NII and servicing-fee beats in Q2 2026 bought -0.5%. The baseline shows only 2 of 7 prints up, so line-level beats have not been paid.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was released this morning, the day before State Street's print. The Zacks key-metric estimates (2026-10-09) predate it and show flat QoQ servicing fees and NII. If priced, State Street would have outperformed today and consensus NII would sit above Q2's $860M. Citi's own stock slipped on its beat (Investing.com headline), so sector tape does not show the read-through being bid.
evidence.independence: This is a proxy, not State Street's number: Citi's mix is more deposit- and payments-heavy. JPM's 8-K (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/JPM/8-k-jpmorgan-chase-co-reports-material-event-6f03387f3670.html), with deposits +2% QoQ and NII +6% QoQ, is a second, broader peer pointing the same way. State Street's CFO said 'stable' on 2026-09-14 (finding 1), which caps the read-through.

evidence.text: Into the print the stock fell -6.79% over 20 sessions to $172.56, 11.2% below its 52w high and well below its 50-day MA of about $186. Over the same 30 days, Q3 consensus EPS rose 0.6% to $3.63 and the company raised its fee guide. That is a de-rating with rising estimates. The only sell-side moves found were target trims (BMO 212->200, Truist 191->190) with ratings kept, and there was no company-specific negative news.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 came into the print near highs after a run-up and fell -0.5% on a beat (the Investing.com call note attributes the muted move to the prior run-up and to expense concerns). This time the setup is the reverse: a lower starting point.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly the opposite of unpriced: the drawdown IS the price. The claim is that the bar for the reaction is lower than in July. If the market were pricing a weak quarter, consensus would have been cut rather than raised 0.6%, and skew would be put-bid rather than -0.22.
evidence.independence: Consensus revision from Zacks via Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ahead-state-street-stt-q3-121501904.html). The cause of the drawdown is unidentified (the absence of an explanation is worth little by itself), so this is sized small.

evidence.text: On the Q2 call State Street flagged about $500M of mostly severance-related one-time costs for its transformation programme. Q1 2026 carried an $89M repositioning charge and Q2 none (10-Q). A further notable charge could land in Q3 or Q4 and would hit GAAP EPS against a $3.63 consensus that most previews treat ex-notables.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance found of State Street's reaction to a repositioning charge alone; the market has usually framed results ex-notable items.
evidence.why_not_priced: Its timing is unknown. If a Q3 charge were expected, previews would show a GAAP vs ex-notable EPS split for Q3. None found does, and the Zacks consensus is a single $3.63.
evidence.independence: The Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093751/000009375126000397/stt-20260630.htm) shows $89M of six-month repositioning charges, all in Q1, so the bulk of the flagged cost is still to come. That is the same programme as this finding, not independent evidence.

evidence.text: The inputs to State Street Investment Management's fees were mixed in Q3. The S&P 500 gained about 2% in Q3 (narrow breadth), and SPY took $22.4B of inflows in the week to 2026-09-25 and $7.7B in the week to 2026-08-21. But global gold ETF AUM fell 7% m/m in September as gold declined, and GLD had outflows in the two most recent weeks. Consensus management fees are $812M vs $772M in Q2 (+5% QoQ), on AUM of $6.375T vs $6.3T at June 30.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 management fees were +29% YoY with $114B of net inflows; the stock reaction was -0.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Weekly flow prints are public; this is a proxy the street models. If analysts had read strong SPY inflows as decisive, consensus AUM would sit well above $6.375T.
evidence.independence: The S&P Q3 return is from First Citizens' Q3 review (https://www.firstcitizens.com/content/dam/firstcitizens/pdfs/wealth/market-outlook/2026/q3-2026-quarterly-market-review.pdf), and the gold ETF data is the World Gold Council figure via search, pointing the other way. The two net to near zero.
